chapter: Regal Theatre, bebop and the Woody Herman date
title: Keeping the beat at the DeLisa and Regal; Gene Ammons and Charlie Parker sitting in
summary: His band stayed rhythmic despite younger players; Gene Ammons played with them at the Regal and Parker often came by after working at the Rum Boogie.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Well, but, wouldn't some of that creep into your band, with the younger musicians wanting to play in that way?

Yeah, we had the freedom and things, but we never did relinquish that beat. We didn't get away from that. We always kept that thing going. And we had plenty -- what's her name played with us, not at the Delisa, but at the Regal, Gene Ammons.
Right. So he was with us, but we always kept that -- and then Charlie Parker, well, he didn't work with us, but he used to come over and play with us all the time.
Right, right. See, he used to work at the Brown Boogie.

Yeah, he used to work over there, and then after he left there,then he would come into Chicago here to play the jazz places.. You remember, they had the 55th Street -- what was that, Ten and Beehive, right, yeah. So all of these different styles and things, with the changing into bebop, but I think that was -- that was my only criticism of the whole thing, is because it changed the public's eyesight of the bands.
